answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Drift Lock. Each identity gets an immutable per-epoch behaviour fingerprint (action mix, timing, counterparties). On a new epoch, an identity must stay within a tolerance band of its own prior history; drifting beyond it caps the account until it re-earns trust over a full reef of slow, consistent activity. Cloned agents share one history, so rotations across a voyage of epochs produce detectable discontinuities.
